notes: Summary: CedarBridge is a mid-to-large retail banking platform embedding a conversational agent for customers and a reranking layer for transaction enrichment. Primary constraint: sub-200ms p95 query latency for short chat turns and <300ms p99 across regions. They are evaluating Redwood Dedicated with private control plane in a VPC and an on-prem fallback for critical workloads. Key ask: guaranteed reserved GPU pool sizing per region + documented failover headroom and SLA credits. Tech preferences: quantized Llama-2-chat or equivalent open models; willing to accept 8-bit quantized variants for cost but wants fallbacks to slightly larger models in cross-region failover.
use_case_summary: workload: customer-facing chat (real-time) + backend reranking for fraud signal enrichment
throughput target: steady-state 400 QPS across global endpoints, peak 1.2k QPS during business events
latency targets: p95 < 200ms for short chats (<=64 tokens), p99 budget <= 300ms; batch reranker p95 < 120ms
multi-region plan: primary us-east-1 pool, secondary us-west-2 for failover, eu-west-1 for EU-resident traffic
reserved planning ask: baseline reserved GPU capacity to cover 75% steady load + 25% hot-headroom for failover (explicit ask: reserve N+X GPUs per region, show compute-to-qps mapping)
SLAs under negotiation: throughput guarantees (tokens/sec and QPS floors), latency SLOs at p95/p99, credit schedule for misses, planned maintenance windows and advance notice
security: VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 + written audit logging retention, US data residency for payment workflows
operational: requirement for per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, tracing hooks for debugging slow tails
